q-138608.problem:
$$
X=[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 3 \\ 7 & 5 & 9\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the observation matrix $X$ above, where the individual observations are given in columns. Find the mean-deviation form of $X.$
q-138608.worked_solution:
Recall that the mean-deviation form of the observation matrix

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}| & | &  & | \\ {x}_{1} & {x}_{2} & ⋯ & {x}_{n} \\ | & | &  & |\end{aligned}]
$$

is given by 

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}| & | &  & | \\ {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} & ⋯ & {b}_{n} \\ | & | &  & |\end{aligned}]
$$

where ${b}_{i}={x}_{i}-m$ for $i=1,2,…,n,$ and $m$ is sample mean vector.

From the matrix, we have that  

$$
{x}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 7\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 9\end{aligned}].
$$

As a result, the sample mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{1}{3}({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}([\begin{aligned}2 \\ 7\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 9\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 21\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} & ={x}_{1}-m=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 7\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 7\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ {b}_{2} & ={x}_{2}-m=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 7\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ {b}_{3} & ={x}_{3}-m=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 9\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 7\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,  the mean-deviation form is

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

q-138615.problem:
$$
X=[\begin{aligned}-5 & -3 & 2 \\ 7 & 5 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the observation matrix $X$ above, where the individual observations are given in columns. Find the mean-deviation form of $X.$
q-138615.worked_solution:
Recall that the mean-deviation form of the observation matrix

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}| & | &  & | \\ {x}_{1} & {x}_{2} & ⋯ & {x}_{n} \\ | & | &  & |\end{aligned}]
$$

is given by 

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}| & | &  & | \\ {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} & ⋯ & {b}_{n} \\ | & | &  & |\end{aligned}]
$$

where ${b}_{i}={x}_{i}-m$ for $i=1,2,…,n,$ and $m$ is sample mean vector.

From the matrix, we have that  

$$
{x}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 7\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

As a result, the sample mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{1}{3}({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}([\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 7\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 12\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} & ={x}_{1}-m=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 7\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\ {b}_{2} & ={x}_{2}-m=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {b}_{3} & ={x}_{3}-m=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,  the mean-deviation form is

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -1 & 4 \\ 3 & 1 & -4\end{aligned}].
$$

X=[−5−32750] Consider the observation matrix X above, where the individual observations are given in columns. Find the mean-deviation form of X.

a
[−3−1431−4]

EXPLANATION

Recall that the mean-deviation form of the observation matrix

X=[|||x1x2⋯xn|||]

is given by

B=[|||b1b2⋯bn|||]

where bi=xi−m for i=1,2,…,n, and m is sample mean vector.

From the matrix, we have that

x1=[−57],x2=[−35],x3=[20].

As a result, the sample mean is

m=13(x1+x2+x3)=13([−57]+[−35]+[20])=13[−612]=[−24].

Now, we have the following:

b1=x1−m=[−57]−[−24]=[−33]b2=x2−m=[−35]−[−24]=[−11]b3=x3−m=[20]−[−24]=[4−4]

Therefore, the mean-deviation form is

B=[−3−1431−4].

q-138627.worked_solution:
Recall that  the sample covariance matrix is given by

$$
C=\frac{1}{n-1}B{B}^{T},
$$

where $B$ is the observation matrix in the mean-deviation form, and $n$ is the number of observations.

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =\frac{1}{4-1}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 5 & -1 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ -1 & 5 \\ 1 & -1 \\ -2 & -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}10 & 2 \\ 2 & 42\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

q-138631.worked_solution:
Recall that  the sample covariance matrix is given by

$$
C=\frac{1}{n-1}B{B}^{T},
$$

where $B$ is the observation matrix in the mean-deviation form, and $n$ is the number of observations.

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =\frac{1}{4-1}[\begin{aligned}0 & 5 & -6 & 1 \\ 10 & -6 & 5 & -9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 10 \\ 5 & -6 \\ -6 & 5 \\ 1 & -9\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}62 & -69 \\ -69 & 242\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

X=[\begin{aligned}4 & 6 & 5 \\ -3 & 0 & 6\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the observation matrix $X$ above, where the individual observations are given in columns. Find the sample covariance matrix of the data.
q-138639.worked_solution:
Recall that  the sample covariance matrix is given by

$$
C=\frac{1}{n-1}B{B}^{T},
$$

where $B$ is the observation matrix in the mean-deviation form, and $n$ is the number of observations.

So, we first need to compute the mean-deviation form of our observation matrix.

The sample mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{1}{3}({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}([\begin{aligned}4 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 6\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}15 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} & ={x}_{1}-m=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -3\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\ {b}_{2} & ={x}_{2}-m=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ {b}_{3} & ={x}_{3}-m=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 6\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,  the mean-deviation form is

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & -1 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, the sample covariance matrix is 

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =\frac{1}{3-1}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & -1 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & -4 \\ 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 3 & 42\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
